name: Winterfell
description: Ancient seat of House Stark and capital of the North, built over hot springs against the winter cold. Burned by Theon's ironborn, seized by the Boltons, retaken by Jon and Sansa — and the field of the Long Night, where the Night King shattered at Arya's hand.

name: Castle Black
description: Principal stronghold of the Night's Watch at the foot of the Wall. Jon Snow rose from steward to Lord Commander here — was murdered and resurrected within its walls — and rode out its gate into the true North in the series' final shot.

name: White Harbor
description: The North's only city and its main port, ruled by House Manderly, bannermen of the Starks. Jon and Daenerys' armies landed here on the march to Winterfell.

name: Moat Cailin
description: Ruined fortress guarding the causeway through the Neck — the choke point between North and South. Held by ironborn until Ramsay Bolton took it back through Theon's surrender.

name: The Dreadfort
description: Grim seat of House Bolton, whose banners carry the flayed man for good reason. Theon Greyjoy was unmade into Reek in its dungeons.

name: Bear Island
description: Forested island in the Bay of Ice, seat of House Mormont. Ten-year-old Lady Lyanna Mormont pledged its sixty-two fighting men to Jon Snow — and died killing a giant at Winterfell.

name: Last Hearth
description: Seat of House Umber, last castle before the Gift and the Wall. The dead reached it first in Season 8 — little Ned Umber was left pinned in the Night King's spiral.

name: Karhold
description: Seat of House Karstark, Stark kin who broke with Robb over Lord Rickard's execution and fought for the Boltons — until Alys Karstark knelt to Jon.

name: Deepwood Motte
description: Wooden motte-and-bailey of House Glover in the wolfswood, seized by Yara's ironborn in the books; the Glovers' wavering loyalty shapes Jon's Season 6 campaign.

name: Torrhen's Square
description: Square keep of House Tallhart southwest of Winterfell. Theon's feint against it drew Winterfell's garrison away in Season 2.

name: Barrowton
description: Town built around the great barrow of the First Kings, seat of House Dustin. Book background in the show.

name: Greywater Watch
description: Floating castle of the crannogmen, moving forever through the swamps of the Neck. Home of Howland Reed — the only living witness to the Tower of Joy — and his children Meera and Jojen.

name: Hornwood
description: Seat of House Hornwood between the Dreadfort and Winterfell, swallowed into Bolton hands in the wars. Book background only.

name: Cerwyn
description: Castle of House Cerwyn a half-day's ride from Winterfell. Ramsay flayed Lord Cerwyn for refusing his taxes — as Sansa is grimly told.

name: Oldcastle
description: Seat of House Locke on the White Knife's mouth. Book background only.

name: Ramsgate
description: Holdfast east of White Harbor. Book background only.

name: Widow's Watch
description: Seat of House Flint of Widow's Watch on the stormy eastern cape. Book background only.

name: Flint's Finger
description: Castle of House Flint on the swampy western cape above Cape Kraken. Book background only.

name: Queenscrown
description: Abandoned tower in a lake in the Gift, crowned in gold for a visiting queen. Bran hid here as Jon, held by the wildlings below, refused to kill an innocent — and wargs saved them both.

name: Mole's Town
description: Village half-buried under the Gift, serving the Wall's less official needs. Ygritte's raiders sacked it in Season 4; Sansa met Littlefinger in its tunnels in Season 6.

name: The Nightfort
description: Oldest and most haunted of the Wall's castles, long abandoned. Bran's party crossed beneath the Wall through its hidden Black Gate; Sam and Gilly sheltered in its kitchens.

name: The Shadow Tower
description: Westernmost manned castle of the Night's Watch, guarding the Gorge. Mentioned as one of the three castles still garrisoned.

name: Westwatch-by-the-Bridge
description: Abandoned Night's Watch castle at the Wall's western end. Book background only.

name: Sentinel Stand
description: Abandoned castle of the Wall's western reaches. Book background only.

name: Greyguard
description: Crumbling Wall castle — the posting Ser Alliser used to exile Janos Slynt, before Slynt's refusal cost him his head.

name: Stonedoor
description: Abandoned castle of the Wall. Book background only.

name: Hoarfrost Hill
description: Abandoned castle of the Wall. Book background only.

name: Icemark
description: Abandoned castle of the Wall. Book background only.

name: Deep Lake
description: Wall castle built to replace the sinister Nightfort. Book background only.

name: Queensgate
description: Abandoned Wall castle named for the queen whose crown gilded Queenscrown. Book background only.

name: Oakenshield
description: Abandoned castle of the Wall east of Castle Black. Book background only.

name: Woodswatch-by-the-Pool
description: Abandoned castle of the Wall. Book background only.

name: Sable Hall
description: Abandoned castle of the Wall. Book background only.

name: Rimegate
description: Abandoned castle of the Wall. Book background only.

name: Long Barrow
description: Abandoned castle of the Wall, built over an old barrow. Book background only.

name: The Torches
description: Abandoned castle of the Wall. Book background only.

name: Greenguard
description: Abandoned castle of the Wall near its eastern end. Book background only.

name: Northern Watchtower
description: Lonely watchtower of the northern hills. Book background only.

name: Northern Holdfast
description: Small holdfast of the northern countryside. Book background only.

name: Crofters' Village
description: Village by a lake in the wolfswood — in the books, the frozen camp of Stannis's final campaign.

name: Tumbledown Tower
description: Ruined tower of the wolfswood. Book background only.

name: Stony Shore Village
description: Fishing village of the Stony Shore — the coast Theon raided to prove himself ironborn in Season 2.
